newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end sharply down on stocks, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end sharply down on stocks, weather.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed sharply lower on bearish input from a government stocks report and from good crop weather, traders said.
"The weather right now is absolutely beautiful," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.
Meteorologists said U.S. Midwest farmers should be able to harvest corn and soybeans this week as drier weather settles over the region and temperatures warm to near normal.
"The Midwest will be in a drier-than-normal pattern during the first half of October," Smith Barney meteorologist Jon Davis said in his daily report.
The market was double teamed, first by the weather then USDA's quarterly stocks report released Monday at 0730 CDT.

USDA said the supply of soybeans in the United States as of September 1 totaled 183.2 million bushels, above an average of analysts' estimates for 163 million and above the highest trade estimate for 175 million bushels.
November early broke below support at $7.79 and again at $7.66 and sell-stops were hit on the way down. Fund selling led the collapse and was countered by scale-down cash demand.
Soybeans closed 11-1/2 to 25-1/4 cents per bushel lower, with November down 25-1/4 at $7.58.

Fund selling totaled at least 25.0 million bushels with Refco Inc the key seller of 10.0 million bushels of November, the traders said. Iowa Grain, Griffin Trading and E.D. and F. Man each sold five million November and Prudential Securities sold six million November, they said.

Commercials were net buyers with Cargill Inc a noted purchaser of five million November, Tenco Inc bought five million November, Continental Grain bought two million November, Farmers Commodities Corp bought 3.5 million November and Produce Grain bought two million bushels of November, traders said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated at 78,000, up from 45,601 Friday, according to the CBOT.

Soybean options trading featured Smith Barney's purchase of 1,000 November $7.75 puts and sale of 1,000 January $7.75 puts at seven cents, the traders said. Smith Barney also bought 2,000 November $7.75 puts and sold 2,000 January $7.50 puts and five to six cents, they said.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 30,000, up from 27,752 Friday.
